newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima gets thumbs up from voters - poll.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima gets thumbs up from voters - poll.

text.p: The choice of Austria's Viktor Klima to succeed Franz Vranitzky as chancellor has improved the Social Democrats' rating with voters and stemmed the flow of votes to the far-right, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.
The change of chancellors has raised the Social Democrats' share of voters by two percent in the last week to 35 percent, according to a Gallup opinion poll printed in current affairs magazine News.
Their junior coalition partner, the conservatives, remained unchanged at 25 percent, while the Freedom Party lost one percent to 26 percent.
The Social Democrats' popularity had waned over the past decade, losing votes largely to Haider's far-right Freedom Party.
Social Democrat Klima, who was chosen last Saturday to succeed Vranitzky, was also the favourite choice should there be a direct election for the chancellorship, the poll showed.

The 49-year-old gained 47 percent, while conservative People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel lagged behind with 14 percent, followed by far-right Freedom Party chief Joerg Haider with eight percent.
Chancellor-designate Klima also scores top marks with voters over his prospects of leading the Alpine republic.

In response to the question "Who should in future play an important political role?", 57 percent chose Klima, putting him well above President Thomas Klestil at 50 percent, and Vice-chancellor Schuessel at 43 percent.
The poll, conducted by Gallup, surveyed 600 Austrians.
